claims.statement: For every s != 0, the supremum over probability densities f with ||f||_infinity <= 1 of |integral exp(i s x^2) f(x) dx| equals 1. Hence no law-uniform pointwise decay envelope tending to 0 exists.
claims.implication: refutes the proposed per-direction law-uniform van der Corput decay step, not the bounded-density conjecture

claims.statement: For independent X1,X2 with densities <=1 and same-sign coefficients lambda1,lambda2 with magnitudes >=1, lambda1 X1^2 + lambda2 X2^2 has density bounded by pi/sqrt(|lambda1 lambda2|) <= pi.
claims.scope: two independent coordinate-square terms with same sign

claims.statement: For Q=sum_j lambda_j X_j^2 diagonal in the original independent coordinates, if at least three |lambda_j|>=1 then Q has density bounded by pi, uniformly in n, laws, signs, repeated eigenvalues and all remaining coefficients.
Extend the universal density bound to arbitrary orthogonal eigenvectors while preserving a dimension-independent constant.
claims.next_obligation: Use product-density structure to average the two-dimensional same-sign coarea bound over the orthogonal complement without paying unnormalized slice volume.
